comment: The missed comparison was D<A: the two-layer GRU beat the narrow three-layer transformer, but not C or the wider transformers. I treated nominal Adagrad progress as sufficient to put every transformer ahead of D. K1075 did not justify that extrapolation: its controlled evidence uses Adam, and it explicitly rejects a universal family cutoff. K1017 helped with B<E but cannot settle GRU–transformer comparisons. History backtesting found matched-rate/decay Adagrad GRUs winning 30/30 comparisons across eight questions at lr≤.0003, versus only 13/24 across five questions at lr≥.001. Lab contained zero fully matched Adagrad cross-family pairs. Initialization and optimization conditioning are plausible, unmeasured explanations; no tested rule resolves this high-rate pair.
